lines.text: How did a chained rebel vanish inside a temple?
In the seventeen fifties, Puli Thevar of Nerkattumseval refused to pay tribute to the Nawab and the British.
lines.caps: in the *1750s | *Puli *Thevar | of *Nerkattumseval | *refused | to pay *tribute | the *Nawab | and the *British

lines.text: Accounts say Yusuf Khan's cannon pounded his fort for weeks. In seventeen sixty one, it fell.
Puli Thevar slipped away. When Yusuf Khan himself was hanged, he came back and took the fort again.

lines.text: Around seventeen sixty seven, British troops under Campbell took it again.
A legend says he was captured, and asked to pray one last time at the temple in Sankarankovil.

lines.text: Guards outside heard iron crack. Inside, they found only broken chains. He was never seen again.

lines.text: School history books say something plainer: he escaped, and died in exile.

lines.text: Others suspect the vanishing tale covered up a quiet execution. None of it is proven.
